summary: Aiko Okoshi worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Kyoto University from around 1970 to 1975, and held a post as a full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Aileen Dansken Ross was an Indologist. She studied at the London School of Economics (B.Sc., ~1936–1939) and the University of Chicago (M.A., Ph.D., ~1939–1951), and held faculty posts at the University of Toronto (1942–1945) and McGill University (1944–1970).

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bedford College (~1974–1977) and trained under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in 2010.

Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Emmanuel College and the University of Cambridge (~1969–1972) and trained under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah. He became abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1995.
Ajahn Khemadhammo, working in Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Drama Centre London (~1963–1966) and trained under Ajahn Chah from around 1972 to 1977.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Ajahn Pasanno studied under traditional teacher Ajahn Chah from around 1974 to 1982. He later served as founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a degree at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971), trained as a disciple under Ajahn Sumedho in 1977, and served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MA at UC Berkeley (~1961–1963) and studied under Ajahn Chah (1967–1977). He served as abbot at Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).
Ajay Verma specializes in philosophy and Indology. He completed his M.Phil. and Ph.D. at the University of Delhi (1997–2004) and became an Associate Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2005.

Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held a post as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.
Akhil Rajeev P works in computational fields and Indology. He has held posts at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1975–1984), Honganji Sōgakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao (1979–2002). His academic posts include Ryukoku University, Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Yuichi Kajiyama, earned a master's at Kyoto University (1976), and a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle / University of Paris (~1979–1983). He held faculty and leadership positions at Kyushu and Kyoto universities.
Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University. He later held positions there, attested as a full-time lecturer in 1992 and as Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2013.
Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies and other fields. She studied as a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and was appointed Professor at Musashino University in 2022.

Akiko Murakawa is an Indologist who completed her studies under supervisors and teachers including Harry Falk, Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, Kazuhiko Yoshida, and Muneo Tokunaga.

Akiko Walley works in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), and held an academic post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Katsumi Mimaki, Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar, and doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn, completing a Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg (attested 2005).
Akio Donohashi works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1968 to 1976 and served as a Professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Minoura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held an associate professorship at Otani University (attested 2007–2013), conducted research abroad at Stanford University (2012–2013), and is attested as faculty at Otani Academic Society in 2026.
